COMPLETE EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN   

======================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary design: Bank-level Difference-in-Differences (DID) with an event-study extension.

• Cross-sectional dimension: Ex-ante vulnerability of the lead bank to the panic—measured before the crisis—captures anticipated supply pressure.  
 – Funding-side shock: reliance on (non-deposit) short-term wholesale funding as of 2007-Q4.  
 – Drawdown-side shock: predicted dollar amount of committed credit lines that will be pulled onto the balance sheet; instrumented with each bank’s 2006–07 revolving-credit commitments interacted with the average August–December 2008 draw-down rate of the borrower’s 3-digit SIC industry (“shift–share”).  

• Time dimension: pre-panic versus post-Lehman (15 Sept 2008) months/quarters.  

DID is appropriate because:
1. The shock was sudden, externally generated (failure of Lehman + run on wholesale funding).  
2. Banks differ markedly and observably in ex-ante exposure; these differences are predetermined and plausibly orthogonal to 2008 loan-demand conditions.  
3. High-frequency DealScan data permit clean before/after comparison and rich fixed effects to partial-out demand shifts.  

Event-study coefficients (τ = -8 … +8 months around September 2008) let us test “parallel-trends” and visualize dynamics.

A secondary IV layer—using predicted rather than realized draw-downs—helps isolate exogenous variation in the liability shock and addresses endogeneity of actual draw-downs.

======================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment 1 (Funding Shock):  
 Treated bank b = 1{ WholesaleFundingRatio_b ≥ 75th percentile of 38 lead banks }  
 WholesaleFundingRatio = (federal-funds + RPs + commercial paper + other short-term non-deposit liabilities) / Total Liabilities, Call Report 2007-Q4.  

Control group: banks below the 75th pct. (robustness: terciles or continuous exposure).  

Treatment 2 (Draw-down Shock):  
 PredictedDrawShock_b = Σ_i (Commitment_{bi,2006-07} × AvgDrawRate_{industry(i),Aug–Dec 2008}) / Assets_b.  
 High-shock = top quartile.  

Timing:  
 Pre = 2006 Q1 – 2008 Q2 (or February 2008 inclusive)  
 Post = 2008 Q4 – 2008 Q4 (quarterly spec) or Sept 2008 – Dec 2008 (monthly spec).  
 Observation unit: bank-quarter or bank-month; outcome = log dollar volume of NEW syndicated loans signed in the period (and alternative extensive-margin dummy).

No RDD—no running variable with cutoff; the shock is discrete in time.

======================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel Pre-Trends: Conditional on fixed effects and controls, high- and low-vulnerability banks followed similar trends in new lending before September 2008.

 Plausibility: Funding structures change slowly; no major wholesale-funding disruptions 2006–08:H1. Pre-trend tests feasible.

A2. Exogeneity of Exposure: 2007 reliance on wholesale funding and credit-line portfolios is predetermined with respect to August–December 2008 loan-demand shocks to the bank’s customer base.

 Plausibility: Funding structure stems from business model and regulatory constraints; borrowers could not foresee Lehman collapse.

A3. No Spillovers/General Equilibrium Contamination: Borrowers turned to safer banks but did not induce those banks to ration more because of binding capital or liquidity constraints.

 Plausibility: Some spillovers possible; we will test for them by checking whether “safe” banks increased originations.

A4. Stable Composition of Borrowers: The set of potential syndicate borrowers per bank does not shift discontinuously for reasons unrelated to supply (addressed via borrower-industry-time fixed effects).

======================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigating Tests  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Differential Demand Shock: Clients of wholesale-funded banks might face worse product-market prospects, so loan demand could fall harder at treated banks.

 Mitigation:  
 – Include borrower-industry × quarter dummies in loan-level spec.  
 – Bank × borrower-industry pre-period shares control.  
 – Firm-level panel (Compustat manufacturers) where we include firm fixed effects and observe each firm’s simultaneous borrowing from multiple banks.

T2. Measurement Error in Treatment: Call-Report funding ratios might be noisy or window-dressed.

 Mitigation: Use multiple snapshots (2006-Q4, 2007-Q4) and continuous treatment; instrument with historical average funding ratios 2004–06.

T3. Other Simultaneous Policy Shocks (e.g., TARP in Oct 2008).

 Mitigation:  
 – Trim sample after Dec 2008.  
 – Control for whether bank received TARP early (interaction with post).  
 – Event-study to show break coincides with Lehman rather than TARP.

======================================================================  
5. R Code Outline (executable)  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(lubridate)
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Load Data ---------------------------------------------------------
deals   <- fread("dealscan_2000_2008.csv")      # loan-level
banks   <- fread("bank_call_2004_2008.csv")     # Call Reports
draws   <- fread("predicted_drawdowns.csv")     # shift–share calc
tarp    <- fread("tarp_acceptance.csv")         # policy control

# 2. Construct Key Bank-Level Variables -------------------------------
banks[, wholesale_ratio := (fed_funds + repo + cp + other_noncore) / total_liab]
banks[, treat_funding  := as.integer(wholesale_ratio >= quantile(wholesale_ratio, .75))]
banks <- merge(banks, draws, by = "bank_id", all.x = TRUE)
banks[, treat_draw     := as.integer(pred_draw_share >= quantile(pred_draw_share, .75))]

# 3. Aggregate Loan Originations --------------------------------------
deals[, sign_date := as.Date(sign_date)]
deals[, ym := format(sign_date, "%Y-%m")]
deals <- deals[purpose != "credit line amendment"]          # keep new money
loan_month <- deals[, .(newloan_usd = sum(facility_amt, na.rm=TRUE)),
                    by = .(bank_id = lead_bank_id, ym)]

# 4. Create Panel ------------------------------------------------------
# Monthly panel for Jan 2006–Dec 2008
months <- data.table(ym = format(seq(ymd("2006-01-01"),
                                     ymd("2008-12-01"), by = "month"), "%Y-%m"))
panel  <- CJ(bank_id = banks$bank_id, ym = months$ym)
panel  <- merge(panel, loan_month, by = c("bank_id","ym"), all.x = TRUE)
panel[is.na(newloan_usd), newloan_usd := 0]
panel[, ln_newloan := log1p(newloan_usd)]

# Merge covariates
panel  <- merge(panel, banks[, .(bank_id, treat_funding, treat_draw,
                                 wholesale_ratio, pred_draw_share)], by="bank_id")
panel  <- merge(panel, tarp, by = c("bank_id","ym"), all.x = TRUE)   # tarp_post indicator
panel[is.na(tarp_post), tarp_post := 0]

# Time dummies & post indicator
panel[, date := ym(ym)]
panel[, post := as.integer(date >= ymd("2008-10-01"))]  # Q4 onset

# 5. Main DID Regression ----------------------------------------------
did_spec <- feols(
  ln_newloan ~ post*treat_funding + 
               post*treat_draw   + 
               tarp_post + 
               controls...,            # placeholder for size, capital ratio, etc.
  data = panel,
  fixef = ~ bank_id + ym,            # bank & month FEs
  cluster = ~ bank_id)

etable(did_spec)

# 6. Event-Study -------------------------------------------------------
panel[, rel_month := as.integer((date - ymd("2008-09-01"))/30.4)]
panel[, rel_month := pmax(pmin(rel_month, 8), -8)]          # bin extremes
es_spec <- feols(
  ln_newloan ~ i(rel_month, treat_funding, ref = -1) | bank_id + ym,
  data = panel, cluster = ~ bank_id)
iplot(es_spec)

# 7. Robustness: Continuous Treatment ---------------------------------
cont_spec <- feols(
  ln_newloan ~ post:wholesale_ratio | bank_id + ym,
  data = panel, cluster = ~ bank_id)
etable(list(DID = did_spec, Continuous = cont_spec))
```

======================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic prior: Banks in the top quartile of wholesale funding will cut NEW syndicated lending by roughly 40–60 percent relative to low-exposure banks in 2008-Q4, holding demand fixed. In logs this implies a coefficient around ‑0.5 to ‑0.9. Predicted draw-down exposure should generate an additional (perhaps smaller) negative effect.

======================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
----------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Pre-period parallel trends documented by flat event-study coefficients …………… 1  
C2: No obvious simultaneous confounders differentially hitting treatment vs control … 0.5  
C3: Treatment exogeneity (predetermined 2007 balance sheet) ……………………………… 0.8  
C4: No interference/spillovers across units ………………………………………………………… 0.5  
C5: Stable composition & measurement of outcome ……………………………………………… 0.9  
Total (out of 5) = 3.7

======================================================================  
This plan leverages predetermined cross-bank heterogeneity and the sharp timing of the Lehman-induced panic to isolate the causal impact of bank funding stress on the supply of large corporate loans.
